The entire core fact set—November 12 cooling-water pressure loss causing unplanned advanced-packaging shutdown, reduced saleable-bit output, revised customer delivery dates, and recovery window through January 31, 2027—is unrecorded and constitutes new information.

candidates.proposition: On November 12, 2026, an unexpected loss of cooling-water pressure occurred in a shared utility loop at Micron Technology's advanced-packaging facility.

As a direct consequence of the cooling-water pressure loss, Micron placed a defined group of advanced packaging tools into a controlled safe state; the interruption was not part of a planned maintenance event.
The affected advanced-packaging area serves selected high-bandwidth-memory (HBM) and server-memory customer programs.
Following its initial review, Micron reduced its expected saleable-bit output for the affected packages during the current recovery period.
Micron adjusted delivery dates for a limited set of customer commitments that had been scheduled to leave the affected packaging sequence before the end of December 2026.

The company stated that the affected output cannot be recovered simply by moving material through the normal weekly maintenance calendar and is not treating the change as a routine sequencing adjustment.

Micron expects the physical repair work on the affected utility loop to conclude during the week of November 18, 2026, followed by staged equipment return, qualification lots, and controlled restoration of normal release volumes.
Based on the current engineering plan, the affected packaging area is expected to remain in recovery through January 31, 2027, extending beyond the site's ordinary planned-maintenance interval.

Micron did not attribute the interruption to demand conditions, customer specifications, or a product-quality issue, describing it instead as an operational disruption at a key manufacturing-support node.
Other manufacturing and packaging areas at the site continued to operate normally during the interruption.
